comparison_protocol: V53 frozen protocol: full-day5 user-crossfit gate, then fit on day5 and evaluate the future day6 cohort; compare paired rows against V53/V50 reference under the recorded history weights.

critical_findings: V61 fits CatBoost on the complete scored cohort (model.fit(x_aug, z['y'])) and predicts that same matrix (predict_proba(x_aug)) on both days. These are training-set AUCs, not held-out estimates; target labels directly participate in model fitting.

The field named v53_auc is computed from z['pred'], the underlying prior prediction, not the final V53 predictor. On the aligned rows it reproduces 0.8176714756 (day5) and 0.8249578084 (day6), while final V53 is 0.8180913841 and 0.8254233319.

The candidate has no V61 frozen manifest binding parameters, source code, input hashes, fit rows, or prediction artifacts, and no independent out-of-sample replay. Existing report labels both outputs as probe and itself says a strict benchmark is still required.

Day5/day6 validation dates and cohorts have been repeatedly reused in prior experiments. Any apparent result on these dates is not an untouched confirmation; V53's own intervals condition on fitted models and do not account for repeated selection or calendar shift.
audit.leakage_boundary: The added context feature aggregates rows strictly before each day cutoff, but that does not cure fitting and scoring on the same target cohort.

day6.protocol: fit on day5; future day6 cohort

next_step: Do not promote or report the V61 probe AUC as benchmark performance. A future test must freeze its recipe and source/input hashes before scoring, use user-disjoint crossfit for the day5 gate, then train only on day5 labels for day6, verify exact event/label alignment and strict pre-cutoff feature timestamps, and disclose date reuse.
